recognize_zh: 背景中散布許多大小不一、圓形、淡藍灰色且無顆粒、邊緣平滑的細胞質碎片（淋巴腺小體，lymphoglandular bodies），旁邊為中型淋巴樣細胞，與血小板相比顏色較淡、無紫紅色顆粒，提示淋巴細胞性病變侵犯骨髓。
features: Numerous small round pale blue-gray agranular cytoplasmic fragments with smooth borders and variable size in the background
Fragments lack the purple granular centers of platelets, allowing distinction from platelets
Cluster of lymphoid cells, mostly small-to-intermediate with round nuclei, condensed chromatin and scant basophilic cytoplasm
Occasional larger cells with more open chromatin and a rim of basophilic cytoplasm
Thick aspirate background with red cells; one segmented/band granulocyte present
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a group of lymphoid cells, predominantly small to intermediate in size with round nuclei, clumped chromatin and scant basophilic cytoplasm, admixed with occasional larger cells with more open chromatin. The background contains numerous round, pale blue-gray, agranular cytoplasmic fragments of variable size with smooth contours, consistent with lymphoglandular bodies; these are distinguished from platelets by their lack of azurophilic granules and paler color. Lymphoglandular bodies are nonspecific but indicate a lymphoid population and are more frequent in marrows involved by B-cell lymphoma. Findings are suggestive of marrow involvement by a lymphoproliferative disorder; flow cytometry and biopsy correlation are recommended.

ddx.vs: Platelets contain central purple azurophilic granules (granulomere) and are more uniform in size, while lymphoglandular bodies are pale, agranular and variable.
Smudge cells are disrupted nuclear material with purple chromatin strands, not smooth-bordered blue cytoplasmic globules.
ALL may also shed cytoplasmic fragments but its cells are blasts with fine chromatin and high N:C ratio, unlike the mostly mature-appearing lymphocytes here; flow cytometry confirms.
